purpose: Record intentional M2A flow-semantics revisions after the behavior-preserving M1 migration.

entries.question: What happens to a direct nullable-variable narrowing after that variable is assigned?
entries.decision: A successful assignment or numeric compound assignment to a direct variable invalidates every active non-null narrowing for that resolved binding. The binding returns to its declared or inferred type until a later supported nil check establishes a new narrowing. The invalidation remains effective in enclosing active flow regions that may observe the mutation, while facts introduced only in a nested region are discarded when that region ends.
entries.m1_behavior: Before this revision, active branch narrowing survived an assignment to the same binding.
entries.rationale: The assignment mutates the shared binding cell, so a prior proof about its value is no longer valid. Clearing the fact is conservative and preserves the existing rule that only direct simple-variable nil checks establish narrowing.
affected_consumers: nullable type-error and positive recheck fixtures
entries.compatibility_consequences: Programs that use a nullable binding as non-null after assigning it must re-check the binding. No parser, IR, bytecode, VM, field/index, loop, post-branch, alias, or call behavior changes in this slice.
entries.migration: Keep the existing branch-fact producer and add scoped invalidation records beside it. TypeChecker records the invalidation only after normal assignment validation succeeds; no duplicate semantic or lowering path is introduced.
entries.quantitative_gate: The m0d-2026-07-22-r1 inventory validates 1662 cases, the focused FlowFacts CTest passes, the named positive and negative fixtures pass, and the full canonical verification command remains the release gate.
entries.old_path_deletion_condition: There is no compatibility implementation to delete in this slice. The old behavior is replaced only after the shared invalidation record and positive/negative mutation fixtures pass.

entries.question: Can a function or closure body inherit nullable narrowing from its definition-site control flow?
entries.decision: No. Every function body is checked with an empty active flow-fact environment. Function parameters and facts established inside the body are still checked normally, while a captured binding is observed through its declared or inferred type until the body establishes its own supported narrowing.
entries.m1_behavior: Before this revision, checkFunctionBody inherited active facts from an enclosing if branch when a nested function was declared there.
entries.rationale: A function may execute after its definition-site branch has ended, and closures observe shared mutable cells. A definition-site proof cannot be treated as a proof at every later call site.
affected_consumers: TypeChecker function, method, and lambda body analysis
nullable closure-boundary type-error and runtime fixtures
entries.compatibility_consequences: Function bodies that relied on an outer nullable proof must add a local nil check or accept the nullable type. This slice does not infer call-site effects or invalidate caller facts when a closure may mutate a captured binding.
entries.migration: Wrap the shared checkFunctionBody entry point in a flow-fact isolation scope so named functions, methods, and anonymous functions use the same rule. Restore the caller state on success and exceptions.
entries.quantitative_gate: The m0d-2026-07-22-r1 inventory validates 1665 cases, the FlowFacts CTest passes, the named function-boundary positive and negative fixtures pass, and the full canonical verification command remains the release gate.
entries.old_path_deletion_condition: Delete no additional production path in this slice. The inherited-fact behavior is removed only after the shared function-body isolation and both compatibility fixtures pass.
